note: Hand-written file contract for the R04 (Abraham) normal enemies D1-D3 and the D3 charge states. Same 32 px rules as art 03 / R02 / R03 (PPU 32, pivot (16,1), art faces right, flipX once on the parent). Gameplay numbers (HP, speed, radius, timings, dash path) belong to Core and the catalog; they are quoted only where a clip's timing depends on them. The D3 danger lane is NOT a PNG: see src/telegraph_r04.json.
pivotSpace: pixel-edge coordinates, origin at the bottom-left corner of one frame cell, x right, y up
frameLayout: one horizontal strip per clip; frame i occupies x = i*cell.w .. (i+1)*cell.w, full height; no padding

flip.note: flip once on the actor's parent (or its single renderer), same rule as art 03 / R02 / R03. D3 windup and dash face the Core locked direction: flipX when its x is negative; vertical charges keep the last facing

alphaPolicies.binary: alpha is 0 or 255 only; RGB is 0 wherever alpha is 0

edgeMargin.why: no opaque pixel in the outer 1 px ring of a frame, so Point filtering and flipX never cut the outline; ground sprites stand on the foot row = cell.h - 1 - pivot.y

assets.use: chase loop. The dust trail is drawn into the clip (puffs kicked up behind the hind feet on frames 1 and 3); no separate ground decal
floating chase loop (bob is inside the frames). No projectile or barrage art: D2 has no barrage in this round
normal chase, and again after each dash

the 1.2 s charge warning, D3 standing still. Driven by the Core warning clock, not by fps: frame 0 (head down, pawing) for warning elapsed 0-0.6 s, frame 1 (reared, gathered) from 0.6 s held until the dash starts. Faces the Core locked direction. Shown together with the procedural lane of src/telegraph_r04.json
the 0.6 s straight dash: loops from the Core dash start until the dash ends, then back to move. Faces the Core locked direction

notProduced.dash lane PNG: not made on purpose: the danger lane is drawn by Unity from the Core projection (src/telegraph_r04.json). A picture must not define or suggest the hit area
notProduced.D1 dust ground decal: not needed for the first slice; the trail is inside the move clip. Make an optional-fx decal only if the Unity screen review asks for a longer trail
notProduced.death / hit clips: not in the R04 brief; the existing shared enemy hit/death handling applies

motifs.source: Genesis 12-14: Abraham's journey through the wilderness and the Negev, and the raid of the four kings who took the goods of Sodom and Gomorrah and Lot (14:11-12). Creative adaptation for the game.
motifs.d1: a lean, dust-coloured wilderness beast that tracks travellers by scent, kicking up dust behind it (a created monster, not an animal named in the text)
motifs.d2: a deceiving lantern spirit: a hanging cage lamp with a sly face and a pink-violet false light that lures travellers off the road (a created monster)
motifs.d3: a riderless raider war-horse with a bone mask, a red raid blanket and saddlebags of plunder (a created monster that stands for the raid, not a soldier or king)
motifs.excluded: Abraham, Sarah, Lot, Melchizedek, Hagar, God, angels and the covenant signs (the smoking fire pot and flaming torch of 15:17, the stars, the altar) are never enemies or enemy effects. No human riders, captives or victims are drawn
